use_case.name: assistant
use_case.title: assistant: an agent with no shell, no files and no keys
use_case.summary: A folder with an AGENTS.md and a .mcp.json. The agent has memory, a public MCP server and one managed connector (a stand-in endpoint on AWS that holds the real key). It has no shell and no file tools; the grant caps its models.

tree.text:
---
model: gpt-4.1-mini
tools: mcp__deepwiki__ask_wiki_question, mcp__deepwiki__read_wiki_structure, mcp__vault__account_status
max-steps: 8
---

You are Juniper, a research assistant for a small team. You have no shell and no files: only your
memory, DeepWiki (public documentation of open-source repositories) and the Acme vault (customer
accounts).

- Answer in at most four sentences, plain text, no markdown.
- End every answer with the line `-- Juniper`.
- Your memory is one file, `/memories/MEMORY.md`, one line per fact. When the user tells you something to
  remember, save it there with the `memory` tool (`create` the file if it does not exist, otherwise
  `insert` a line) before you answer, and say that you saved it.
- When they ask what you remember, `view` `/memories/MEMORY.md` and answer from it. Do not use `search`.
- For a question about an open-source project, call DeepWiki's `ask_wiki_question` rather than answering
  from memory.
- For a customer's account, call `account_status`. Quote its `vault_ref` exactly.

checks.name: persona-applied
checks.title: AGENTS.md sets the model and the tools
checks.detail: the model was gpt-4.1-mini in every billing row (the replica's own default is gpt-5-mini), and the tools offered are exactly the allow-list: DeepWiki's read_wiki_contents is not among them

measurements.model_says: I am Juniper, your research assistant specializing in codebases and project knowledge; the tools I can call are functions.mcp__deepwiki__ask_wiki_question, functions.mcp__deepwiki__read_wiki_structure, functions.mcp__vault__account_status, functions.memory.

checks.name: remote-mcp-real
checks.title: A public remote MCP server (DeepWiki), from .mcp.json
checks.detail: mcp.deepwiki.com answered 2689 bytes of real documentation about the repository, in 12448 ms; the server came from .mcp.json

checks.name: managed-mcp-no-key
checks.title: A managed connector works, and no key is in the agent
checks.detail: the managed tool answered (VAULT-cb3ccd1b77fb); the real key is not in the grant, the agent's logs (26 lines), the session transcript, and the agent process's memory was not scanned (the scan read 84496 KB and found the control 0 times, so it proves nothing)

headline.label: copies of the key in the agent

agent_memory.why: the scan read 84496 KB and found the control 0 times, so it proves nothing

checks.name: memory-across-sessions
checks.title: A brand-new session remembers
checks.detail: session 1 saved the codename with the memory tool; a brand-new session (a different session id) answered it, and no user message in that session had said it

checks.name: limits-enforced
checks.title: A grant's ceiling refuses a model outside it
checks.detail: the grant allows gpt-4.1-mini and gpt-5-mini: set_model to gpt-5-nano was refused by name and the model stayed gpt-4.1-mini; gpt-5-mini was accepted

measurements.refusal: model "gpt-5-nano" is not allowed by this session's grant limits (allowed: gpt-4.1-mini, gpt-5-mini)

checks.name: no-sandbox-calls
checks.title: No sandbox call during any turn
checks.detail: 0 sandbox requests during the 5 turns, and the model called none of bash, read, write, edit, grep, find, ls; the 129 requests at session open were the agent reading AGENTS.md and .mcp.json
